title: Regular-word identification after forgetting the external action
statement: Use quasicategories and coherent diagrams as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], monoidal infinity-categories as in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], and the planar operad $\mathsf{Chain}_2$ and its operator category as in [lem-coef-composable-bimodule-operad-segal]. Let $\mathcal V$ act coherently on $\mathcal M$, let $A$ be an associative unital algebra of $\mathcal V$, and let $Q$ be a coherent left $A$-module of $\mathcal M$. Let $F$ be the regular operadic lift encoding the $(A,A)$-bimodule $A$ and the module $Q$: its restriction to $\mathsf{BM}_{01}$ is the algebra $A$ composed with the map of planar operads $\mathsf{BM}_{01}\to\mathsf{Ass}_1$ sending $a_0,p,a_1$ to $a_1$ and each operation to the unique operation of the same arity (so both actions on $p$ are multiplication, with all unit and associativity coherences), and its restriction to $\mathsf{BM}_{12}$ encodes $Q$. Let $R$ be the category with objects $pa_1^nq$ for $n\geq0$ and all endpoint-preserving block operators retaining $p$ and $q$. Let $W$ be the category with objects $a_1^kq$ for $k\geq0$ and all endpoint-preserving block operators retaining $q$. Relabelling $p$ as $a_1$ defines a functor $r:R\to W$. Evaluate both restrictions of $F$ by total-contraction cocartesian transport of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] in the underlying category $\mathcal M$; denote the resulting diagrams by $Y:N(R)\to\mathcal M$ and $X:N(W)\to\mathcal M$. There is a coherent equivalence $Y\simeq X\circ N(r)$, with components identifying $A\otimes A^{\otimes n}\otimes U_AQ$ with $A^{\otimes(n+1)}\otimes U_AQ$, compatible with every string of operators in $R$. The diagram $X$ is defined on all of $N(W)$, including the leading-unit arrows $a_1^kq\to a_1^{k+1}q$ whose first output block is empty; these arrows are not in the image of $r$. These comparisons are in $\mathcal M$ after forgetting the external left action and assert no $A$-linearity of a leading-unit insertion. No colimits are assumed.
